title: openai-bridge-v5: preserve determinism hints and annotated metadata in Responses compatibility
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Bridge: Add support for forwarding OpenAI-style determinism hints and annotated metadata from Responses variants. Improves streaming reassembly robustness and preserves toolcall headers for function/tool routing.
description:
Motivation: New OpenAI Responses variants expose two practical features we need to support in the compatibility bridge: (1) determinism hints that affect rerolling/seeded inference (not always a raw numeric seed), and (2) an annotated metadata envelope that clients expect to be passed through back to their application layer. Without preserving these we see mismatch between Redwood responses and customer expectations (reproducibility and attribution).

What this PR does: Adds a compatibility layer in the OpenAI bridge that: 1) accepts the newer 'determinism_hint' top-level field (and the legacy 'seed' when present) and maps both into an internal safe representation (x-rdwd-determinism-hint) which is forwarded to the serving runtime and persisted with the response event. 2) accepts an 'annotations' / 'metadata' object from incoming Responses-style requests, validates it against a white-list (string keys, small scalar values) and forwards it as an opaque envelope into our response records and emitted events. 3) improves streaming reassembly by introducing "liveness anchors"—small sequence markers attached to partial events so the client can reconstitute ordered structured outputs even when chunks arrive out of order. 4) ensures tool/function calling headers (x-rdwd-toolcall-id, x-rdwd-toolcall-wrap) are carried through the bridge to the tool runtime and mapped back into the OpenAI-compatible "tool_call" frames so SDKs receive function call events as expected.

Compatibility and fallbacks: The bridge recognizes multiple Response variants via a 'response_variant' flag (v1/v2/v5). For older requests we fall back to prior behavior. For determinism, if both 'seed' and 'determinism_hint' are provided we prefer the explicit 'determinism_hint' and log an inspector warning. Customers using Redwood Dedicated with strict determinism can pin a deterministic profile; the bridge now surfaces the upstream hint for audit and replay.

Design notes (high level): - Minimal surface: use header translation (x-rdwd-*) rather than changing core request schemas. This keeps the runtime agnostic and limits blast radius. - Validation: annotations are size-limited (max 2KB serialised), keys must match ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$, values must be strings or numbers. Invalid annotations are dropped and a warning returned in the response 'warnings' array. - Streaming anchors: binary-safe 8-byte anchor appended to the metadata of each partial event. Receiver reassembly uses anchor order, then sequence index. Anchor collisions are rare and cause a compact re-fetch of the missing shard. - Toolcall mapping: toolcall headers are stable strings; we generate a synthetic 'tool_origin' attribute that ties the function invocation back to the original request's metadata envelope.

Tests and CI: Added unit tests in bridge tests covering mapping and validation, integration tests that spin up the openai-compat harness and verify function-call roundtrips, and an e2e streaming test that simulates chunk reordering and validates reassembly. Also added a small dedicated load test that measures latency impact of anchor embedding (negligible in our quick runs).

Commits (summary): - Add compatibility translator for determinism_hint and seed -> bridge/header mapping - Validate and forward annotations envelope to events store - Implement liveness anchors for streaming reassembly and consumer helper - Propagate toolcall headers through bridge to tool runtime and back to OpenAI frames - Tests: unit + integration + streaming e2e harness - Docs: how-to and compatibility notes in docs/openai_compat.md

Files changed (high level): ["src/bridge/openai_compat.ts", "runtime/stream/anchor_reassembly.go", "api/handlers/toolcall_proxy.py", "docs/openai_compat.md", "tests/bridge/test_determinism.ts", "tests/integration/test_toolcall_roundtrip.py", "tests/e2e/test_stream_anchor_reassembly.sh", "pkg/events/annotations.go", "pkg/events/events_store_migration.sql", "ci/workflows/openai-compat.yml", "examples/openai/response-variant-samples.json", "README.md"]

Patch snippet (illustrative, kept tiny):
const mapped = {
  headers: {
    ...incoming.headers,
    'x-rdwd-determinism-hint': incoming.body.determinism_hint || incoming.body.seed || undefined
  },
  metadata: validatedAnnotations(incoming.body.annotations)
};

Review conversation (condensed):
- Arjun Patel: "Nice focused change. Two asks: (1) can we avoid adding anchors to every single token event by coalescing them when streaming rate is > 200 RPS? (2) add stronger unit tests for malformed annotations."
- Maya Singh (author): "Answer: we coalesce anchors when rate threshold hit (see runtime/stream/coalesce.go left-in). Added more tests for malformed keys and oversized payloads."
- Sofia Reyes: "Please confirm metrics emitted for dropped annotations and the inspector warning shape. Also check security review for arbitrary metadata size/keys."
- Maya Singh: "Metrics added: bridge.annotations.dropped and bridge.annotations.accepted. Security: white-list + size limit. I ran a short audit and added doc note."
- Ben Kwan: "Integration passed locally but CI hit a flakey test on macos runner (socket timeout). Rerun fixed it."
- Arjun Patel: "LGTM after semantics clarified on deterministic precedence. Approving now."

CI status history: initial CI run: lint pass, unit tests pass, integration tests fail (timeout on test_toolcall_roundtrip.py), rerun integration -> pass, workflow green. Coverage delta: +0.6%.

Notes for release: This change is non-breaking for the vast majority of users. Customers that depended on silently dropping unknown top-level fields should verify their clients if they rely on exact payload shapes. We added two documented headers (x-rdwd-determinism-hint, x-rdwd-toolcall-id) and the annotations envelope behavior to docs/openai_compat.md.

Related: ENG-1429 (compatibility with Responses v5), ENG-1587 (structured streaming reassembly).
